meta.methodology: Read framework.md, the 3 edges with reference===216 from torahData.js (all eitza type), and the full source text torah_216.txt. Because there are zero bechina edges in the dataset for Torah #216, the 'additions' analysis focuses on: (1) bechina statements in the source text that are not captured as bechina edges; (2) dataset nodes for Torah #216 that are not yet assigned to a package; (3) concepts in the source text with explicit bechina language that would constitute new nodes. Only statements with bechina markers (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, נִקְרָא, קוֹרִים, 'זֶה') were considered as bechina candidates.

A bechina edge between these two nodes should be added to reference 216.

analysis_notes.summary: Torah #216 is an extremely compact single-pulse teaching (2 sentences) with no bechina edges currently in the dataset. All 3 existing edges are eitza. The source text contains exactly one explicit bechina marker ('וְזֶה בְּחִינַת') establishing that the 18 blessings ARE the nullification of nature. A second bechina-type identity (הטבע = אם כל חי) is expressed through the philosophers' naming. The teaching's architecture is a clean two-package structure: good (prayer/18 blessings as nature-transcending force) vs. evil (nature/determinism/heretics as the worldview that prayer overturns). The most significant gap is the absence of הטבע, אם כל חי, and המינים/אפיקורסים as standalone bechina-connected nodes in the dataset.
